title: New Zealand's National Cyber Security Centre warns of advanced AI threats
source_used: The420.in (write-up of the NCSC warning); pool item MLex is paywalled and returned no text
key_facts: New Zealand's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) warns that AI is changing the cyber threat environment, making attacks faster, more scalable and potentially more personalised.
The NCSC says AI is already part of the criminal toolkit, making phishing, scams and social engineering more convincing.
The NCSC warns that future AI models could automate attacks and find vulnerabilities, and that tools limited to leading frontier models could reach malicious actors by early 2027.

The NCSC handled 369 incidents of potential national significance in 2025-26, a 16.2 percent increase; four were classed as C2 (highly significant), the same as the total at that level over the previous 10 years combined.
Catriona Robinson, head of the NCSC, says cyber security is a board-level issue; the article says basic security practices still block many AI-enabled attacks.
quote_evidence: The NCSC said it handled 369 incidents of potential national significance during 2025-26, a 16.2% increase compared with the previous year.
"Government cannot protect every organisation from every cyber threat," Robinson said.
why_it_matters_hint: Attackers can use AI to speed up and personalise attacks, and New Zealand's incident count is rising.
